```python
def show_scaling_strategies():
    """Display scaling strategies"""
    print_header("📈 SCALING STRATEGIES")
    
    print("""
VERTICAL SCALING (Scale Up)
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
    Before:           After:
    ┌──────┐         ┌──────┐
    │4 CPU │    →    │16 CPU│
    │8 GB  │         │64 GB │
    └──────┘         └──────┘
    
    ✅ Simple to implement
    ✅ No code changes
    ❌ Limited by hardware
    ❌ Single point of failure
    ❌ Expensive

HORIZONTAL SCALING (Scale Out)
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
    Before:           After:
    ┌──────┐    ┌──────┬──────┬──────┐
    │Server│ → │Srv 1 │Srv 2 │Srv 3 │
    └──────┘    └──────┴──────┴──────┘
    
    ✅ Cost effective
    ✅ High availability
    ✅ Unlimited growth
    ❌ More complexity
    ❌ Data consistency challenges

DATABASE SCALING
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
    
    1. Read Replicas:
       ┌────────┐
       │ Master │ ← Writes
       └───┬────┘
           │
      ┌────┼────┐
    ┌─▼─┐ ┌▼─┐ ┌▼─┐
    │R1 │ │R2│ │R3│ ← Reads
    └───┘ └──┘ └──┘
    
    2. Sharding:
    Users 1-1M    → Shard 1
    Users 1M-2M   → Shard 2
    Users 2M-3M   → Shard 3
    """)
```

Display SQL vs NoSQL comparison

```python
def show_database_comparison():
    """Display SQL vs NoSQL comparison"""
    print_header("🗄️ DATABASE COMPARISON")
    
    print("""
┌──────────────────┬─────────────────┬─────────────────┐
│                  │      SQL        │     NoSQL       │
├──────────────────┼─────────────────┼─────────────────┤
│ Data Model       │ Tables, Rows    │ Key-Value, Doc  │
│ Schema           │ Fixed           │ Flexible        │
│ Scalability      │ Vertical        │ Horizontal      │
│ Transactions     │ ACID            │ BASE            │
│ Consistency      │ Strong          │ Eventual        │
│ Query Language   │ SQL             │ API/Query Lang  │
│ Best For         │ Complex queries │ High scale      │
│ Examples         │ MySQL, Postgres │ MongoDB, Dynamo │
└──────────────────┴─────────────────┴─────────────────┘

When to use SQL:
✅ Need ACID transactions
✅ Complex queries with JOINs
✅ Structured, relational data
✅ Data integrity is critical

When to use NoSQL:
✅ Massive scale (millions of users)
✅ Flexible schema
✅ High write throughput
✅ Horizontal scalability needed
    """)
```

```python
def show_cache_strategies():
    """Display caching strategies"""
    print_header("💾 CACHING STRATEGIES")
    
    print("""
CACHE LAYERS
━━━━━━━━━━━━
    User Request
         ↓
    ┌─────────────┐
    │   Browser   │ ← Client cache
    └──────┬──────┘
           ↓
    ┌─────────────┐
    │     CDN     │ ← Static content
    └──────┬──────┘
           ↓
    ┌─────────────┐
    │    Redis    │ ← Hot data
    └──────┬──────┘
           ↓
    ┌─────────────┐
    │  Database   │ ← Persistent storage
    └─────────────┘

CACHE EVICTION POLICIES
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

1. LRU (Least Recently Used)
   ┌─────────────────┐
   │ A → B → C → D   │ Most recent →
   └─────────────────┘
   Remove A (oldest access)

2. LFU (Least Frequently Used)
   ┌─────────────────┐
   │ A:5 B:3 C:8 D:2 │ Access count
   └─────────────────┘
   Remove D (lowest frequency)

3. TTL (Time To Live)
   Remove after expiration time
   Best for: Session data

CACHE PATTERNS
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

1. Cache-Aside (Lazy Loading):
   App → Check Cache → Miss → Load DB → Update Cache

2. Write-Through:
   App → Write Cache + DB simultaneously

3. Write-Behind:
   App → Write Cache → Async write to DB
    """)
```

```python
def show_capacity_estimation():
    """Display capacity estimation formulas"""
    print_header("📊 CAPACITY ESTIMATION")
    
    print("""
KEY FORMULAS
━━━━━━━━━━━━

1. QPS (Queries Per Second):
   QPS = (DAU × Actions per day) / 86,400
   Peak QPS = QPS × 2

   Example:
   100M users × 10 actions = 1B requests/day
   QPS = 1,000,000,000 / 86,400 ≈ 11,574
   Peak QPS ≈ 23,148

2. Storage Estimation:
   Total = Users × Data per user × Replication factor
   
   Example:
   1B users × 10MB photos × 3 replicas
   = 30,000,000 GB = 30 PB

3. Bandwidth:
   Bandwidth = QPS × Average response size
   
   Example:
   10,000 QPS × 100KB = 1,000,000 KB/s
   = 1 GB/s = 8 Gbps

QUICK CONVERSIONS
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Power of 2:
  2^10 = 1 KB  = 1,024 bytes
  2^20 = 1 MB  = 1,048,576 bytes
  2^30 = 1 GB  = 1,073,741,824 bytes
  2^40 = 1 TB
  2^50 = 1 PB

Time:
  1 day = 86,400 seconds
  1 month ≈ 2.6M seconds
  1 year ≈ 31.5M seconds

LATENCY NUMBERS
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
  L1 cache         0.5 ns
  L2 cache         7 ns
  RAM              100 ns
  SSD read         150 μs
  Disk seek        10 ms
  Network (DC)     0.5 ms
  Network (cross)  150 ms
    """)
```

Display CAP theorem

```python
def show_cap_theorem():
    """Display CAP theorem"""
    print_header("⚖️ CAP THEOREM")
    
    print("""
You can only pick TWO out of three:

        Consistency
           /  \\
          /    \\
         /      \\
        /   CA   \\
       /          \\
   CP /____⚠️____\ AP
     /              \\
Partition          Availability
Tolerance

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

CP Systems (Consistency + Partition Tolerance):
  • MongoDB
  • HBase
  • Redis
  → Sacrifice availability during partition
  → All nodes see same data

AP Systems (Availability + Partition Tolerance):
  • Cassandra
  • DynamoDB
  • Riak
  → Sacrifice consistency
  → Always available, eventual consistency

CA Systems (Consistency + Availability):
  • PostgreSQL (single node)
  • MySQL (single node)
  → No partition tolerance
  → Single point of failure
    """)
```

sections.title: show_load_balancing()

Display load balancing algorithms

```python
def show_load_balancing():
    """Display load balancing algorithms"""
    print_header("⚖️ LOAD BALANCING")
    
    print("""
ALGORITHMS
━━━━━━━━━━

1. Round Robin
   Req1 → Server1
   Req2 → Server2
   Req3 → Server3
   Req4 → Server1 (repeat)
   
   ✅ Simple
   ❌ Doesn't consider server load

2. Least Connections
   Always send to server with
   fewest active connections
   
   ✅ Better load distribution
   ❌ Slightly more complex

3. IP Hash
   Same client → Same server
   hash(client_ip) % num_servers
   
   ✅ Session persistence
   ❌ Uneven distribution possible

4. Weighted Round Robin
   More capacity → More requests
   
   ✅ Handles different server sizes
   ❌ Needs capacity configuration

LOAD BALANCER LAYERS
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Layer 4 (Transport):
  • Fast, operates on TCP/UDP
  • Cannot see HTTP content
  • Good for: High throughput

Layer 7 (Application):
  • Operates on HTTP level
  • Can route based on URL, headers
  • Good for: Content-based routing
    """)
```

```python
def show_quick_tips():
    """Display quick tips"""
    print_header("💡 QUICK TIPS FOR SUCCESS")
    
    print("""
DO's ✅
━━━━━━
  1. Always clarify requirements first
  2. Start with simple design, then scale
  3. Use numbers to back your decisions
  4. Draw clear diagrams
  5. Think about failure scenarios
  6. Discuss trade-offs explicitly
  7. Ask for feedback during interview

DON'Ts ❌
━━━━━━━━━
  1. Don't over-engineer
  2. Don't skip calculations
  3. Don't memorize solutions
  4. Don't ignore constraints
  5. Don't forget to communicate
  6. Don't rush to implementation

KEY PHRASES TO USE
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
  "Let me clarify the requirements..."
  "Based on these numbers..."
  "The trade-off here is..."
  "We could use X, but that would mean Y..."
  "To handle this scale, I would..."
  "A potential bottleneck could be..."
    """)
```
